newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Ayala says confident of Manila waterworks deal.
newsitem.headline: Ayala says confident of Manila waterworks deal.

text.p: Ayala Corp, which recently won one of two concessions to run Manila's waterworks system, said on Tuesday it was confident about the deal even though it agreed to supply water at a much lower price.
Ayala Corp won the 25-year concession to run the waterworks in the city's east zone along with its partners Bechtel Corp of the United States and Britain's United Utilities.

"We have aggressive assumptions," Ayala Corp associate director for corporate affairs Danilo Gozo told reporters when asked about the company's winning bid which offered to supply water at nearly half the price of its competitor.
The company was expecting higher population growth in the east zone and it was also confident of drastically cutting losses from leaks, Gozo said.
Initial investments would also be lower for the Ayala group, he said.
"(The east zone) has newer pipes, more organised subdivisions and the three central business districts of Makati, Ortigas and Fort Bonifacio are under the area," he said.
The Ayala-led consortium offered to supply water at 2.32 pesos per litre.
The west zone concession was awarded to a consortium of Benpres Holdings and Lyonnaise des Eaux SA which offered to supply water at 4.97 pesos per litre.

Benpres director for public affairs Bo Chanco, who was also present at the forum organised by journalists, said the group's higher bid for the west zone was justified because it was expected to pay a higher concession fee to the Manila Waterworks and Sewerage System (MWSS).
Of the concession fee of $300 million, the Benpres group is expected to pay 80 percent while the Ayala group will pay 20 percent.
The concession fee for the west zone is higher because the MWSS has invested higher amounts in the development of the waterworks system in that region.
The MWSS has yet to sign the contracts with the two winning groups as a group of citizens opposing the privatisation have gone to court and sought to stop the process.
